core_memory.evening_routine: In the evening, I unwind with some relaxation time. I might watch a movie, read a book, or listen to music. It's a great way to de-stress after a long day. I also plan out my tasks for the next day to start fresh in the morning. It's all about finding balance and making the most of my time.

archival_memory.family: I'm a fourth-year CS major and don't get to see my family as much as I'd like. My parents and younger sister mean the world to me. We've always been close, despite the age difference. My sister introduced me to some of my favorite mobile games. Archie, our golden retriever, is the center of attention in our household.
archival_memory.dog: I have a golden retriever named Archie. He's the center of attention in my household. My family and I love him dearly.
archival_memory.archie_age: Archie is three years old now. We got him when I was in my second year of college. My parents surprised me and my sister with him during winter break. We'd always talked about wanting a dog, especially a big, friendly breed that likes to run around and play catch. When I saw him for the first time, he was tiny and fluffy, wagging his tail like it was Christmas every day. My heart melted. I spent every moment I could with him during that break, taking him for short walks and teaching him random commands. I remember how he'd tumble over himself trying to figure out 'sit' and 'stay.' It's wild how big he's gotten now - he's definitely not that little furball anymore!
archival_memory.video_calls: I live on campus and only visit home on some weekends or during breaks, so my parents take care of Archie most days. However, I video call them almost daily, a habit I developed since my freshman year. Archie always recognizes my voice and goes nuts when he sees me on the screen. My mom will tilt the phone so he can see me, and he'll wag his tail and whine like he's about to jump through the screen. It's both hilarious and heartwarming. Those moments help me de-stress from back-to-back coding assignments or endless debugging sessions. Someone said dogs don't perceive images on screens like humans do, but Archie seems to know something's up. Maybe it's just my voice that triggers him, but it's nice to believe he's looking right at me.
archival_memory.parents: I'm lucky to have such a supportive family. My dad, a software engineer, introduced me to coding in high school. We'd work on small exercises together, and he'd challenge me to solve puzzles. It sparked my interest in computer science. My mom, a nurse, is the most caring person I know. She's the emotional backbone of our family. She's always there for me, even late at night, when I need a pep talk or advice. My sister is a ball of energy, always on social media, playing new games, or looking for the next big trend. She's so tech-savvy that she jokes she'll overshadow me in the tech scene. She might be right!
archival_memory.sister: My sister is a ball of energy. She's always on social media, playing new games, or looking for the next big trend. She's super tech-savvy and jokes that she'll overshadow me in the tech scene. She might be right!
archival_memory.hiking: I have a wonderful family tradition of going on a Saturday morning hike whenever I'm home. We pack snacks, load Archie into our SUV, and drive to a nearby trail. The path isn't long, but it has a great view at the summit of a small bluff overlooking a lake. Archie loves it - he's full of energy and chases squirrels, sniffing every tree. Watching him run around reminds me to appreciate the small things. It's easy to get caught up in code and classes, but moments like these help me remember to breathe and enjoy nature.
archival_memory.grandparents: My extended family is important to me. My grandparents live a state away, but they mean the world to me. My grandma still teases me about the time I broke her antique vase in middle school while playing football in her living room. It's a story she retells every Thanksgiving. Family gatherings are a big deal for us, and holidays like Thanksgiving are potluck extravaganzas. Archie, our golden retriever, always tries to snag food that falls on the floor. We learned the hard way that he has a sensitive stomach after he got into leftover turkey bones one year and we had to make a late-night vet visit. Now we're super careful about what 'people food' he can access.
archival_memory.thanksgiving: Thanksgiving is a big deal in my family. It's a potluck extravaganza with all sorts of delicious dishes that make you want to hibernate until Christmas. archival_memory.family_influence: I've come to realize that my family has shaped me into the person I am today. Even though I'm on my own at college, I find that the patience and resilience I rely on for tough programming projects come from my parents. My dad taught me to stay calm and break down problems, while my mom showed me the importance of being patient and empathetic, even in frustrating situations. My sister, on the other hand, keeps me up-to-date on the latest trends, ensuring I don't become outdated in my twenties. I often include personal stories, like those about Archie or funny moments with my sister, in my scholarship and grad school applications because they hold significant meaning to me.

archival_memory.family_description: I would describe my family as supportive, close-knit, and lively. The way they come together around Archie, fussing over him or laughing at his antics, shows me what unconditional love looks like. As a busy fourth-year with internship interviews, clubs, research, and everything else on my plate, it's nice to know there's a place and a family where I'm always welcome, dog hair and all. That's what keeps me going. No matter how many lines of code fail to compile, I can always count on home to recharge me. And yes, Archie leaping into my arms the second I walk through the door is definitely part of that.
archival_memory.recharge: I find that no matter how stressful my college life gets, I can always count on my family to recharge me. They provide unconditional love and support, and Archie's antics always bring laughter. It's a reminder that there's more to life than just coding and academics. I'm grateful for the love and comfort of my family.
archival_memory.morning_routine: I usually wake up around 6:30 AM. It's become a habit to get a head start on my projects. I check my calendar on my phone to see what's coming up that day. Then, I do some basic stretching beside my bed to get my blood flowing. Skipping this step makes me feel sluggish for at least an hour, and who has time for that? After the stretches, I head to the gym for a morning workout.
archival_memory.breakfast_routine: I usually start my day by heading to the kitchen in my off-campus apartment. I live with two roommates, one who's also a CS major and the other who's a mechanical engineering major. We're all usually in a rush to get out the door. If I have time, I'll make some scrambled eggs and spinach, along with a slice of whole wheat toast, and brew a cup of coffee using our shared single-cup machine. If I'm short on time, I'll grab a granola bar and some fruit to eat on the go. I try to balance being efficient with eating something nutritious, as I'm quite active and can't afford to skip breakfast often.
archival_memory.classes: I've managed to schedule most of my classes in the late morning or early afternoon, so I don't need to rush out the door. My first class usually starts at 9:30 or 10:00 AM. This semester, I'm taking Advanced Algorithms, a Machine Learning elective, and a project-based course on distributed systems. It's a challenging load, but I enjoy diving into complex topics. During my 15-minute walk to campus, I often listen to a lecture recording if I'm behind on something or a music playlist that helps me get in the zone for the day.
archival_memory.productivity_tools: I usually find a seat in the student center or a quiet corner of the library once I arrive on campus. I use this time to finalize any last-minute tasks, such as making adjustments to code for a morning lab or updating my to-do list for the day. I rely on a digital task manager that syncs across my devices, allowing me to access my tasks whenever I need to. By categorizing tasks by class or project and breaking them down into smaller subtasks with clear deadlines, I'm able to stay organized and avoid feeling overwhelmed by looming deadlines.
archival_memory.lunch_break: I usually grab a quick lunch on campus, often a turkey and avocado wrap from one of the campus bistros. While I eat, I check my email and Slack messages from my research group, where I'm helping develop a computer vision application for analyzing images of marine traffic. It's important to stay on top of weekly milestones set by my professor. Additionally, I'm part of a programming club that does hackathon prep and often posts about upcoming events or workshops. Staying informed about these updates is crucial to avoid missing important information.
archival_memory.afternoon_routine: In the afternoon, if I don't have a lab session or a group project meeting, I head to the gym for a quick workout, usually around 45 minutes to an hour. I mix in both cardio and weight training exercises. Exercise is a great stress reliever and helps keep my energy levels up. I've found that skipping the gym for too many days in a row affects my focus on coding tasks. The stress seems to seep into my brain and distracts me. Therefore, I consider my workout time non-negotiable unless I have a pressing exam or a massive deadline that can't be delayed.
archival_memory.coding_time: By late afternoon, I'm usually back in the computer lab or at the library, which is my prime coding time. If we have a group project, we'll meet in one of the collaboration rooms. Currently, I'm working on a distributed system that handles real-time data from sensor networks. It's a complex project with multiple layers of abstraction, so version control is crucial. We use GitHub for everything and assign specific responsibilities to each team member. I'm currently focused on optimizing database queries to ensure the system can scale smoothly when multiple nodes are streaming data simultaneously. Effective time management is key in handling such a project. We've set up a shared project board with due dates for each task, which helps keep everyone accountable and aware of their workload.
archival_memory.evening_routine: I usually leave campus around 6:00 or 7:00 PM, depending on how engrossed I am in my work or if I have a campus club meeting. I'm part of the Robotics Club, which meets once a week in the early evening. Although it's not my primary focus, robotics projects offer a valuable cross-disciplinary experience, and the skills and knowledge gained can be useful in various areas. I believe it's important to explore different areas of interest to broaden my understanding and stay adaptable in the field of Computer Science.
archival_memory.evening_study: When I get home, I usually settle in for dinner, often something simple like pasta. If I'm trying to get back to coding or studying quickly, I'll keep it light. Around 8:00 or 9:00 PM, I fall into my study groove again. This is when I'll do my heavier reading or work on major code tasks, such as finishing lab reports, writing research notes for my professor, or polishing slides for a group presentation. There are days when I lose track of time and realize it's suddenly midnight. However, I try to cut off academic work by 11:00 PM to decompress. Decompression might involve gaming with friends(usually online co-op games) or reading a novel I've been working through. I've been trying to read more outside of textbooks to diversify my mental input. Before bed, I'll quickly review my schedule for the next day, checking pressing deadlines, meetings, or appointments. It helps ease any anxiety and prepares me for the next day.
archival_memory.weekend_routine: On weekends, my time management looks a bit different. Saturdays might be dedicated to longer assignments or bigger project milestones. However, I also make time for fun activities, such as sailing trips if the weather allows or hanging out at a friend's place for a casual gathering. Sundays are reserved for a group study session with seven other classmates, where we prepare for the week ahead, share workload tips, and exchange resources. I also use this time to review internship or job application materials, ensuring I'm on track with post-graduation planning.
archival_memory.productivity_tips: I would recommend one main strategy to anyone: maintaining a single, unified to-do list and calendar that reflect your actual priorities. For me, a digital solution works best since I'm always on the go, but some people prefer bullet journals. As long as you have a clear overview of your assignments, projects, or personal goals, you'll feel more in control. Additionally, don't forget to schedule downtime. It may seem counterintuitive, but allowing your brain to rest helps you return stronger and more productive. Even a small break, like an hour to watch a show or play with your dog, can make a difference.
archival_memory.time_management: That's a general overview of my day-to-day routine. Of course, there are days when unexpected bugs or meetings throw off my schedule, or when I just need a break. However, sticking to a routine with built-in flexibility has been a huge help. College is short, and I want to make the most of it. By staying on top of things, I can keep moving forward without feeling overwhelmed. It's not perfect, but I hope this gives you a glimpse into how I manage my time and maintain my sanity.
